title: U.S. House · Illinois's 3rd District
area: Parts of Chicago's Northwest and Southwest Sides and western Cook County suburbs

context.text: Incumbent Delia Ramirez (D) ran unopposed in the March 17, 2026 Democratic primary. Angel Oakley won the Republican primary unopposed.

candidates.name: Delia Ramirez
candidates.ballotNote: Ran unopposed in the March 17, 2026 Democratic primary

summary.text: Ramirez has represented Illinois' 3rd Congressional District since January 2023. Before Congress she spent nearly two decades in the nonprofit sector and served two terms in the Illinois House of Representatives (2019-2023), where she co-founded the House Progressive Caucus. She is seeking re-election after an unopposed March 2026 primary.

background.text: Born in Chicago and, according to her official biography, the daughter of working-class Guatemalan immigrants and a lifelong resident of the Humboldt Park neighborhood.
Earned a bachelor's degree in justice studies from Northeastern Illinois University.

Spent 18 years in nonprofit work, according to her official biography: executive director of the Center for Changing Lives, campaign manager at Common Cause Illinois, and deputy director of Community Renewal Society. Ballotpedia also lists her as a social services administrator, community organizer and policy advocate, and a co-founder of Justice for Our Neighbors (JFON).
Served as board chair of the Latin United Community Housing Association (LUCHA) and the Logan Square Neighborhood Association (LSNA).

Elected in 2018 to the Illinois House of Representatives, 4th District, and served 2019-2023. Her official biography says she co-founded the Illinois House Progressive Caucus, became an Assistant Majority Leader in her second term, and lists among her legislation Medicaid coverage for seniors regardless of immigration status, funding for affordable housing and an elected Chicago school board.
Elected to the U.S. House in 2022 and took office January 3, 2023, succeeding Marie Newman. Her official biography describes her as the first Latina elected to Congress from Illinois and the Midwest.
Serves on the House Committee on Homeland Security and the Committee on Veterans' Affairs, where she is the top Democrat on the Subcommittee on Oversight and Investigations.

Her official biography says she is the only member of Congress in a mixed-status family, is married to Boris, and lives in Chicago. She ran unopposed in the March 17, 2026 Democratic primary (72,443 votes).

priorities.text: Housing is a human right, period. As a housing organizer, I know that a new future for housing is possible: one that is bold, progressive, affordable, sustainable. In Congress, I am organizing and fighting for legislation and investment to realize a progressive vision of affordable, sustainable housing for all, by tenants and for tenants.

In one of the wealthiest nations of the world, no person should have to choose between getting the care they need or staggering medical debt, buying their medication, or paying their mortgage. Health care is a human right, full stop.

Know that in me, you will always find someone who stands ready to fight for working families and to protect and support all workers' right to have fair wages, safe and dignified working conditions, universal health care, and democracy in their workplace.

positions.summary: Says she is a long-time advocate for reproductive rights and safe abortion access, and is committed to codifying Roe v. Wade into law.
positions.quote: Representative Ramirez is committed to protecting bodily autonomy and make of Roe V. Wade the law of the land through legislative fix.

positions.summary: Cosponsors gun violence prevention legislation, including Ethan's Law and the Break the Cycle of Violence Act.
positions.quote: As a co-sponsor of Ethan's Law , the Keep Americans Safe Act , and the Break the Cycle of Violence Act , she advocates for gun violence prevention policies that address the root causes of crime and programs that strengthen community violence prevention and interruption.

positions.summary: Calls for abandoning current border enforcement policies and opposes scapegoating asylum seekers, while supporting legal pathways and relief for undocumented immigrants.
positions.quote: Congresswoman Ramirez advocates we abandon the decades of failed border enforcement policies and support for ineffective initiatives and reject the scapegoating of asylees seeking safety.

positions.summary: Champions Medicare for All and led the expansion of Illinois Medicaid to cover residents regardless of immigration status.
positions.quote: As a member of the Congressional Progressive Caucus, Congresswoman Ramirez fights for the passage of the Medicare for All Act , Close the Medigap Act , and the Medicare Dental, Vision, and Hearing Benefit Act.

positions.summary: Cosponsors the Green New Deal and Climate Resilience Workforce Act and calls for ending reliance on fossil fuels.
positions.quote: Ramirez believes we must protect our sacred lands, oceans and wildernesses and end our reliance on fossil fuels.

positions.summary: Says the tax code shouldn't do more for billionaires and corporations than for working families and cosponsors the Tax Excessive CEO Pay Act.
positions.quote: Congresswoman Ramirez believes our tax code shouldn't do more for billionaires and corporations than it does for working families.

record.text: Assigned to the House Committee on Homeland Security and the House Committee on Veterans' Affairs (Subcommittees on Disability Assistance and Memorial Affairs, and Economic Opportunity) in the 118th Congress.

candidates.name: Angel Oakley
candidates.ballotNote: Ran unopposed in the March 17, 2026 Republican primary

summary.text: Oakley is a Republican entrepreneur and consultant with degrees from Judson University and a career spanning technology consulting, cannabis and CBD advising, and teaching as an adjunct instructor. She ran as a write-in independent for this seat in 2024 and was unopposed in the 2026 Republican primary; in her Ballotpedia survey she describes herself as a fiscal conservative who would join the bipartisan Problem Solvers Caucus.

background.text: Earned a bachelor's degree from Judson University in 2004 and a master's degree from Judson in 2013; also graduated from the Illinois Institute of Art.

Career experience includes work as a technology and consulting startup founder, partner and chief marketing and management consultant, cannabis educator and advisor, CBD broker, patient advocate and adjunct instructor; Ballotpedia lists her profession as entrepreneur.

In her 2026 Ballotpedia survey she says she has 30+ years of experience across business, healthcare, technology, manufacturing and education in the district, and has mentored youth, coached robotics, and served as a Village Commissioner, Trustee and Youth Ambassador in Germany. She also says she is a wife of 25 years and mother of three.
Ran as an independent write-in candidate for Illinois' 3rd District in 2024, receiving 96 votes; Delia Ramirez won that election with 67.3% over Republican John Booras.
Advanced from the unopposed March 17, 2026 Republican primary to the November general election.

priorities.text: Lists restoring constitutional freedoms and ending the surveillance state as a policy priority.
priorities.quote: Restore and protect our Constitutional freedoms, and end the surveillance state.

priorities.text: Lists promoting peace accords and refocusing military efforts on homeland defense as a policy priority.
priorities.quote: Promote peace accords. End the wars, and refocus our military efforts on defending our homeland.

priorities.text: Lists reducing the influence of money in politics, including a proposed WIEE Act, as a campaign message.

statements.quote: We should streamline asylum and immigration courts so cases receive timely, consistent decisions, while prioritizing the removal of dangerous criminals.
statements.context: In her WTTW 2026 voter guide answers

statements.quote: I'd protect a fair safety net for those in real need.
statements.context: In her WTTW 2026 voter guide answers, on health care costs

statements.quote: I'd close special-interest loopholes, simplify filing, and keep tax relief focused on working families and job creators.
statements.context: In her WTTW 2026 voter guide answers

statements.quote: Congress has an important role because it controls legislation, funding, and oversight powers allow it to shape long-term foreign policy rather than simply reacting to international crises.

researchNotes: Angel Oakley's statements come from her WTTW voter-guide answers and her Ballotpedia Candidate Connection survey and campaign-website excerpt. Her answers do not directly take a side on most guide issues, so no positions are recorded; her words are shown as statements. Delia Ramirez's positions and priorities are drawn from her official House issues pages. Ramirez's positions and priorities are drawn from her official House issues pages, and her biography from her official House 'About' page and Ballotpedia. Oakley's biography and statements come from her Ballotpedia profile and 2026 Candidate Connection survey (self-reported); no independent news profile or campaign website text beyond Ballotpedia's quotations was found, and the survey's local offices (Village Commissioner, Trustee) were not independently verified.
